author: eBible.org
title: World English Bible, Protestant 66-book edition (engwebp)
location: Matthew 5; Mark 7; Galatians 2–5; Romans 3, 7, 8, 10, 13; Acts 15; Luke 6, 12, 16, 18, 19; Mark 10, 12, 14; Matthew 6, 19, 25; 1 Corinthians 16; 2 Corinthians 8–9; Romans 12, 15; Acts 4; 1 Timothy 6; Luke 8, 10, 24; John 4, 20; Matthew 28; Romans 16; 1 Corinthians 11, 14, 16; Galatians 3; Philippians 4; Acts 18; 1 Timothy 2–3; Titus 2
note: Chapter links in passage records point to this edition. Biblical text is linked, not republished in this repository.

author: Matthew V. Novenson
title: Law in the New Testament
location: Sections 2 ('Christ the end of the law') and 5 ('I have not come to abolish the law')
note: Discusses diversity within Paul and Matthew, including the possibility and limits of interpreting Matthew as a response to Pauline ideas.

author: Bradley M. Trout
title: The nature of the law's fulfilment in Matthew 5:17: An exegetical and theological study
location: Abstract; discussion of fulfilment and kingdom; Conclusion
note: Proposes a salvation-historical/kingdom interpretation of Matthew's fulfilment language. Interpretive proposal, not consensus.

author: Logan Williams
title: The Stomach Purifies All Foods: Jesus' Anatomical Argument in Mark 7.18–19
location: Abstract; sections on Mark 7.18–19 and alternative parsing
note: Argues against the conventional narrator-gloss reading of Mark 7:19c. One recent scholarly case, not a settled correction of all translations.

author: Matthew Thiessen
title: Paul and the Gentile Problem
location: Publisher abstract only (full monograph not checked)
note: Represents a Gentile-focused reading of Paul's legal arguments. Do not cite unseen chapters or pages.

author: American Bible Society
title: The Council in Jerusalem
location: Comparison of Acts 15 with Galatians 2
note: Accessible comparative overview; distinguish Acts as narrative from Paul's first-person letter.

author: John M. G. Barclay
title: Rich Poverty: 2 Corinthians 8.1–15 and the Social Meaning of Poverty and Wealth
location: Full article: Introduction; Macedonians' Wealth-in-Poverty; Corinthians and Christ; Conclusions, especially discussion of 2 Cor 8:1–15
note: Full open-access article inspected. Interprets wealth in 2 Corinthians 8 in terms of giving and social relations, and explicitly cautions against pressure on poor donors.

author: L. L. Welborn
title: ‘That There May Be Equality’: The Contexts and Consequences of a Pauline Ideal
location: Publisher abstract only; full article behind access restriction
note: The abstract describes an ideal of economic equality in collection practices. No claims are made about detailed arguments on inaccessible pages.

author: Louis Ndekha
title: Praising the poor and blaming the rich: A panegyric reading of Luke 6:20–49 in Malawian context
location: Full online article; Abstract, discussion of Lukan blessings and woes, and context-specific application
note: A contextual reading using Greco-Roman praise and blame conventions; its Malawian application is one interpretive perspective, not universal scholarly consensus.

author: H. C. van Zyl
title: Discernment as 'not knowing' and 'knowing': a perspective from Matthew 25:31–46
location: Full online article, especially §2 (identity of 'least'), §3 (not knowing), and discussion of universal and particularist readings
note: Reviews both particularist and universal interpretations of 'the least of these', proposing an integrated reading.

author: Elizabeth Shively
title: Commentary on Mark 10:17–31
location: Full online commentary: context, rich man, and radical discipleship
note: A pastoral/lectionary commentary, not represented as a peer-reviewed journal article. Describes the particular man and broader call to self-denial.

author: Adam Kubiś
title: The Poor Widow's Mites: A Contextual Reading of Mark 12:41–44
location: Publisher abstract and bibliographic record only; full PDF not independently checked
note: The abstract argues for the widow as a positive example and acknowledges a competing negative/exploitation reading. Do not attribute unseen argumentation or page-specific claims.

author: Marieke Sybrandi
title: Women leaders lost in translation? A Study in Romans 16:1–16
location: Full article: Phoebe (vv.1–2), Prisca (v.3), Junia (v.7), translation and conclusion
note: Open full article inspected. Argues that translation/reception history has often minimized women's roles; this is a substantive scholarly interpretation, not a settled identification of modern offices.

author: Michael H. Burer and Daniel B. Wallace
title: Was Junia Really an Apostle? A Re-examination of Rom 16.7
location: Publisher abstract only: argument about epīsēmos en tois apostolois
note: Abstract challenges an inclusive 'outstanding among apostles' reading in favor of 'well known to the apostles'; do not attribute unseen pages.

author: Curt Niccum
title: The Voice of the Manuscripts on the Silence of Women: The External Evidence for 1 Cor 14.34–5
location: Publisher extract and bibliographic metadata only; discusses lack of manuscript omission and verse transposition
note: A contrary critical perspective to interpolation theories; only publisher extract inspected. The full apparatus and article still require direct verification.

author: Joseph A. P. Wilson
title: Recasting Paul as a Chauvinist within the Western Text-Type Manuscript Tradition: Implications for the Authorship Debate on 1 Corinthians 14.34-35
location: Full article: abstract, background, Western-text discussion, and conclusions
note: Argues for a quotation/refutation hypothesis over interpolation while criticizing Western transmission and anti-Judaic assumptions. Represents one debated position.

author: D. Francois Tolmie
title: Tendencies in the interpretation of Galatians 3:28 since 1990
location: Full article: sections on other biblical texts, gender, social implications and history of interpretation
note: Surveys divergent scholarship on spiritual unity and the question of social or ecclesial equality; avoids imposing one conclusion on Galatians 3:28.

author: Raymond F. Collins
title: Pastorals
location: Publisher introduction/extract only: history of authenticity debate and critical authorship consensus
note: Only the accessible Oxford introduction inspected. It documents dispute and critical skepticism about Pastoral authorship; the full bibliography was not accessed.

author: Bible Fellowship Church Study Committee
title: Report of the Study Committee on the Role of Women in the Church, 1 Timothy 2:12 — Majority
location: Full publicly accessible majority report, especially creation-order reasoning and elder-specific teaching restrictions
note: Explicitly confessional/denominational complementarian argument, not an independent academic consensus. Included as a substantial restriction-oriented counterreading.

author: Armin D. Baum
title: Paul's Conflicting Statements on Female Public Speaking (1 Cor. 11:5) and Silence (1 Cor. 14:34-35): A New Suggestion
location: Publisher summary and bibliographic record only
note: A contextual reconciliation proposal; full argument not independently inspected, and this source should not be cited for claims about unseen pages.

author: Felix Just, S.J., Ph.D.
title: The Gospel according to Matthew: Five Major Discourses of Jesus
location: The Structure of Matthew's Gospel and the five discourse comparison tables
note: Accessible chapter/discourse outline and candidate parallel-reference tables. Used as a research aid; listed parallels are not verified quotations, proof of historical independence, or a settled account of synoptic literary dependence.

author: Yale Bible Study, Yale Divinity School
title: The Gospel of Luke — Introduction to the Course
location: Public introduction and 'Structure of the Gospel of Luke' sections
note: Accessible overview of Luke–Acts, Gospel composition, distinctive stories and a literary outline; source-divergence hypotheses remain academic positions, not independently proven conclusions here.

author: Dirk Jongkind
title: Luke 22:43–44. Is the Angel and the Sweat like Drops of Blood an Early Addition?
location: Open research essay: Greek manuscript witnesses, arguments for omission/inclusion, and conclusion
note: Full text read. Explains why THGNT retains the verses marked uncertain while NA28 rejects their originality; a scholarly institutional essay, not a peer-reviewed journal article or proof of one textual solution.

author: Dirk Jongkind
title: 'Father forgive them' — the variant in Luke 23:34a
location: Open research essay: competing manuscript evidence and arguments for omission or inclusion
note: Full text read. Author favors inclusion despite substantial early omission evidence; preserve contrary readings and do not present the editorial decision as consensus.
